sections.h2: Which Lumpkin County offices do what?
sections.html:
Two offices sit at 99 Courthouse Hill in Dahlonega, a few suite numbers apart. One handles value and exemptions. The other handles billing and collection.

Lumpkin County property tax offices

Tax CommissionerBilling, collection, payment questions99 Courthouse Hill, Suite E, Dahlonega, GA 30533706-864-2666; weekdays 8:00am to 4:30pm, closed 1:00pm to 1:30pm; fax 706-867-6010

Source: Lumpkin County Tax Commissioner FAQ page and the county's Assessor's Office page.

Owners can search, view and pay property tax on the commissioner's site. The commissioner sends bills to homeowners only. Lenders do not receive them, so an owner with escrow should pass the bill along.

sections.h2: What should a Lumpkin County seller know about the local population and homes?
sections.html:
Dahlonega is the address for Lumpkin County's tax offices. In its mid-2025 estimate the Census Bureau gives the county 36,178 residents, 8.0% more than its 2020 starting figure of 33,486. The county has about 283 square miles of land, and in 2020 it held 118.4 people to the square mile.

The housing numbers set Lumpkin apart from its three neighbors in the QuickFacts comparison. Owners occupy 76.3% of homes, the top rate among the four places compared, and the middle price of those homes is $307,900 in the 2020 through 2024 data, far above the $174,500 shown for Macon-Bibb County. The household income midpoint is $77,448, with 13.0% of people below the poverty line.

Lumpkin skews older, with 20.6% of its people past 65 against 9.7% in Long County. Age matters for tax relief here, because several exemptions in the county's flyer begin at 62 or 65. QuickFacts shows 14,302 housing units and 270 permits issued in 2025. A commute averages 28.3 minutes.

sections.h2: What does Lumpkin County bill, and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
December 1 is the due date for houses, land and business equipment. The commissioner's FAQ explains that the date was December 20 until the county commissioners signed a resolution in December 2009 moving it up.

  • After the due date, a 5% penalty arrives at the 120 day mark and returns every 120 days until the total reaches 20%.
  • Past 90 days late, a tax fifa (lien) can go on record at the courthouse.
  • Levy on the property is possible, though the FAQ calls it a last resort.
  • Credit bureaus can see the lien, and the tax office says it cannot control their use of it.

Mobile homes run on their own calendar, so an owner of one should phone 706-864-2666 for that date. A location permit is issued only after the current year's mobile home tax has been paid in full.

sections.h2: Which appeal routes exist for a Lumpkin County value?
sections.html:
Three routes appear in the county's flyer, and each begins with a written appeal filed 45 days or sooner after the notice date. Grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, uniformity, or a refused exemption.

  • Board of Equalization: the assessors look first and may revise the value in a new notice, which the owner has 30 days to contest. Otherwise it goes automatically to a hearing, and Superior Court is the next stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser takes value or uniformity disputes on non-homestead real property above $500,000, or on certain wireless property above that same level.
  • Arbitration: the owner submits a certified appraisal, and the assessors either accept it or certify the appeal to the Clerk of Superior Court for arbitration.

The state provides a uniform appeal form, and you name your chosen route in that first written filing. Unsure which fits your case? Call the assessors at 706-864-2433 before filing.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments does Lumpkin County list?
sections.html:
The standard state homestead exemption subtracts $2,000 from assessed value, set by law at 40% of market value. You qualify by owning the home and living in it on January 1. Applications can go in all year, but one received after April 1 starts with the following year. Owners who reach 62 can apply for an additional exemption.

The county's tax information flyer, last dated 2021, also describes local and special programs. Ask the assessors to confirm the current amounts, since those figures may have changed.

  • School tax break for owners 62 and over whose federal adjusted gross income is at most $20,000: $30,000 off assessed value.
  • Owners 65 and up, or permanently disabled: as much as $120,000 off for school tax and $60,000 off for county tax, covering the home and at most 5 adjoining acres.
  • Agricultural preferential assessment: qualifying land is assessed at 30% instead of the usual 40%, under a 10-year covenant that carries penalties if broken.
  • Forest land conservation use: 200 acres or more in total, with parcels of 100 acres or more inside the county.
  • Tax deferral: owners 62 or older with household income under the flyer's $15,000 line can postpone the tax, which is different from an exemption.

A conservation use application (PT-283A) needs a notary's signature and must go in by April 1 with a $25.00 recording fee, because the original is recorded at the courthouse. A senior application should enclose a state ID showing birth date and address, and a disabled veteran application needs the VA letter showing a 100% combined rating.

sections.h2: What are Lumpkin County's assessors doing on the ground?
sections.html:
A posted notice from the Assessor's Office says field inspections are under way countywide, and it cites state law as the authority. Appraisers carry identification, drive marked vehicles, measure exteriors, take photographs and note improvements. Entering a home is generally unnecessary, and owners need not be present.

A second notice on the page says McCormick Solutions, a division of LMC, Inc, will do commercial and industrial appraisals for the board. Its staff wear county-issued badges, and owners may ask to see them.

Forms can be downloaded from the state revenue department's site and mailed in, and the assessors ask for a USPS postmark no later than April 1. These include the state homestead form, the business personal property return (PT-50P), the freeport application (PT-50F), the marine (PT-50M) and airplane (PT-50A) returns, and PT-50R, the taxpayer return of value used to ask for a review.

sections.h2: Who pays the Lumpkin County bill if you sell?
sections.html:
State law puts the full year on whoever owned the parcel January 1, and the revenue department says a mid-year sale earns no refund.

Before listing, phone the commissioner at 706-864-2666 and ask what is still owed on the parcel, interest or lien included. Hand that number to the closing attorney. An unpaid fifa has to be cleared first. A bill that still reaches you after closing should go to the buyer.

An inherited, tax-delinquent or rented house goes through the same sequence.Ask the assessors early whether a senior exemption or deferral is attached to the account, since it can change what is owed at the closing table.

faqs.q: On what date is Lumpkin County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 1, per the commissioner's FAQ. Before a December 2009 resolution by the county commissioners, the usual date had been December 20.

faqs.q: How long is the Lumpkin County dispute window?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice date. Send a written filing to the assessors at 99 Courthouse Hill, Suite C, and say which route you pick.

faqs.q: Does Lumpkin County send my bill to my mortgage company?
faqs.a: No. Bills go to the homeowner, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account should send a copy to the mortgage company.

faqs.q: When must a Lumpkin County homestead application arrive?
faqs.a: The assessors need it ahead of April 1 for it to count this tax year. A later one starts with the following year.

faqs.q: Which office should a Lumpkin County seller call first?
faqs.a: Start with the commissioner at 706-864-2666 to learn what is owed. Use the assessors at 706-864-2433 for value or exemption questions.
